neighbours.label: the manner or companion word right after a verb of going or coming (go quietly, came quietly, went with, go down in history), versus the same words after verbs that are not about going
fire: The old senator said he would not go quietly when the party asked him to retire.
After the argument, the boy went quietly to his room and shut the door.
At sixteen she went with her aunt to Chicago to study music.
The captain decided to go down with the ship as the crew rowed away.
Late at night the cat came quietly through the open kitchen window.
Fans hope the team will go down in history as the best of the decade.
The guests left early, but my brother went with them to the station.
When the police arrived, the thief came quietly and did not resist.
quiet: The old senator said he would not argue quietly when the party asked him to retire.
After the argument, the boy sat silently in his room with the door shut.
At sixteen she studied with her aunt in Chicago to learn music.
The captain decided to stay aboard the ship as the crew rowed away.
Late at night the cat purred softly by the open kitchen window.
Fans hope the team will be remembered as the best of the decade.
The guests left early, but my brother talked to them at the station.
When the police arrived, the thief smiled calmly and did not resist.

predictions: fire 0.3-1.0 on the word after go/went/came; the same word after a non-motion verb below 0.2
